scope: The maintained case qualifies a three-stage HBT transimpedance core over the declared nominal DC corners and the 1 MHz to 100 MHz low-frequency transfer band. The extraction boundary includes candidate-derived HBT geometry and distributed interconnect R/C; no RF transmission-line, EM, noise, or 40 GHz result is implied.

native_extraction.klayout: Strict named-port LVS retains the finite ptap1 card, all four-terminal HBT substrate nodes, and the declared Nx values. The candidate post-layout extraction disables only the KLayout tap model card so the standard Magic sub! body boundary can be reconciled.
native_extraction.magic: Magic supplies distributed interconnect resistance and capacitance. Its compact-device substrate boundary is reconciled through the reviewed HBT merge to VSS; no internal Magic node name is used by the simulator deck.
native_extraction.approved_boundary: The finite source tap remains an explicit model element. The ideal-body post-layout boundary is recorded in backend identity and is calibrated against the finite source deck with the same testbench, models, temperature, and three input-current points.

calibration.method: Run the same source testbench, pinned typical models, temperature, and -100 uA/0 A/+100 uA points for the finite source tap, the source deck with XSUBTAP changed to R=1e-6, and the KLayout-native compact netlist extracted from the candidate with tap extraction disabled.

repeatability.transform: Translate the complete witness by 13 um in X and 17 um in Y on the layout database grid.

limitations: This case does not claim 40 GHz bandwidth, low-noise behavior, RF matching, S-parameters, EM accuracy, substrate resistance accuracy, PVT, mismatch, or linearity outside the three declared nominal input-current points.
The three-point DC sweep is a functional corner check and is not a compression or large-signal linearity characterization.
